headline: Search and generative models now optimize mRNA codons, UTRs and RNA folds
label: Computational Nucleotide Sequence Design
summary: Three May 2026 preprints apply evolutionary, discrete diffusion, and Monte Carlo search to multi-objective nucleotide sequence design.
synthesis: The three preprints share a common design pattern: a learned or generative sequence prior is coupled with a search procedure to optimize several sequence objectives at once. Two address mRNA therapeutics. One pairs a pretrained CodonTransformer with a genetic algorithm to optimize codon sequences for translation, stability, and low immunogenicity. The other, mRNAutilus, jointly designs codons and untranslated regions via masked discrete diffusion with Monte Carlo Tree Guidance, extending guided generation beyond codon-only optimization. The third, Montparnasse, applies Monte Carlo search with nested rollout policy adaptation to RNA design and reports that it solves all Eterna100 V1 puzzles faster than DesiRNA. What is new is the explicit multi-objective framing and the joint codon-UTR design, while the RNA work is benchmarked on search efficiency against an established baseline.
